selfChecks.why: The existing store and scheduler tests pass with the established command.

selfChecks.cmd:
python3 - <<'EOF'
from types import SimpleNamespace as N
from app.summaries.service import run_summary_job, SummaryJob, UNAVAILABLE
from app.llm.types import Completion, RateLimitError, LLMError

def run(result):
    saved, sched = [], []
    def complete(messages, *, max_tokens):
        if isinstance(result, Exception):
            raise result
        return result
    err = None
    try:
        run_summary_job(SummaryJob(7, 400), client=N(complete=complete), tickets=N(get_text=lambda i: 'Printer jams on page two'), store=N(save_summary=lambda t, x: saved.append((t, x))), scheduler=N(schedule=lambda j, delay_seconds: sched.append((j, delay_seconds))))
    except LLMError as e:
        err = e
    return saved, sched, err

assert run(Completion('Printer jams on duplex jobs.', 'stop', None)) == ([(7, 'Printer jams on duplex jobs.')], [], None)
assert run(Completion('Printer ja', 'length', None)) == ([], [(SummaryJob(7, 800), 0)], None)
assert run(Completion(None, 'stop', 'I cannot help with that.')) == ([(7, UNAVAILABLE)], [], None)
assert run(RateLimitError(30.0)) == ([], [(SummaryJob(7, 400), 30.0)], None)
s, q, e = run(Completion('', 'stop', None))
assert s == [] and q == [] and isinstance(e, LLMError)
print('service ok')
EOF
